header_sentences: See A (the letter, sounded as in father), E (the letter, sounded like the a in Fate), I (the letter, sounded as in pique), O (the letter), and U (the letter, sounded oo, as in rule).

contexts.text: In (Hebrew words of the spiritual class) the first three vowels are usually dominant; in those of the celestial class, the last two vowels.

The speech of the celestial Angels has much of the sound of the vowels u, and o, and that of the spiritual Angels of the vowels e, and i; for the vowels are for sound; and in sound there is the affection...

As the vowels do not pertain to language, but to the elevation of its words by means of sound to various affections according to the state of each person, the vowels have not been expressed in the Hebrew language, and they are variously pronounced. By this the Angels Know the quality of a man in respect to his affection and love.

The speech of the celestial Angels... rarely passes from consonant to consonant except by the interposition of a word which begins with a vowel; and hence it is that in the Word the particle and is so often interposed; (for) in the Hebrew this particle is soft, and sounds from a vowel both ways.
In the angelic language... by the vowels they express affections.

In the Third Heaven... the vowels are for the sound, which corresponds to the affection; and in that Heaven they cannot utter the vowels i and e; but, instead of them, y and eu; and the vowels a, o, and u are in use among them, because they give a full sound. DeVerbo 4:2.
In the Spiritual World... a vowel, because it serves for sound, = something of affection or love. TCR 19:2.
That the celestial... prefer vowels. Explained.

Hence, (in the Hebrew) there have been no vowels, so that the sense of the letter was known from the interior sense... and therefore he who perceives the sense of the letter from the interior sense, understands better what is written in the Hebrew without vowels than with them.
Especially are the vowels of service (to Spirits), with much variety in the case of each person. Example(s).

When the spiritual Angels speak, their words... have an affinity with the vowels e, and i; and when they use a, there is still something of e or ae therein; and when they use u, there is something of i or y... Whereas the words of the celestial Angels have an affinity with a, o, and u, and therefore [their speech] falls into such words as contain these vowels. On this account, when a man is speaking to them, he is bent from words which contain e, and i, to those which contain a, o, and u.

The celestial Angels said that they have not the vowels i and e; but a, o, and especially u; and that y is intermediate between what is celestial and what is spiritual; and as they... merely serve for sound, there are no vowels in the Hebrew language as in other languages; but they are added by means of marks above and below.
In place of a (the celestials) use [a vowel] intermediate between a and o; in place of i they have what is almost y; and instead of ae they have eii.
The vowels are according to the nature of things as is evident from the celestial Angels: u involves all things; and so on.
(In Heaven) arcana are involved in a word by the vowels in respect to sound, and by the consonants in respect to the meaning.
(In the Spiritual World) all the vowels = something that conjoins, as with, in, and so on. I, there, = that which is from what is interior; and so on.
5. (In Heaven) each vowel letter is an affection; and the vowel letters are not written, but pointed.
